kjv: Our Father which art in heaven ... Thy will be done, as in heaven, so in earth.
mine: Father, may your name be kept holy. Your kingdom come.
note: TR expands Luke's shorter prayer to match Matthew 6:9-10, adding "hemon ho en tois ouranois" and "genetheto to thelema sou ..."; P75, Vaticanus and others (with Origen's explicit testimony) have Luke's own five-petition form.
TR adds "alla rysai hemas apo tou ponerou" from Matt 6:13; absent from P75, Sinaiticus (first hand), Vaticanus, L.

kjv: If a son shall ask bread of any of you that is a father, will he give him a stone?
note: TR adds the bread/stone pair from Matt 7:9; absent from P45, P75, Vaticanus.

kjv: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites!
note: TR adds "grammateis kai pharisaioi hypokritai" from Matthew; absent from P75, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, C, L.
anaideia is "shamelessness" (lack of regard for propriety), which may describe the asker's boldness or, as some argue, the sleeper's concern to avoid shame.
